title: [finding] `manifestIdRefusal` never says each segment must start with a letter, so `com.example.2app` satisfies every clause of its sentence and is refused
body:
Filing gate: **① a defect with a named landing site**: `manifestIdRefusal` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts`, the refusal sentence `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` answers with. Finding class **(c)**: an AI trap. An author following the stated rule writes a value the regex refuses, and the refusal cannot say why. This is the same defect class as #19831 (`manifest.namespace`), on the sibling key that card's dispatch ruled out of scope.

Found by the `os-dev` round on #19831 (PR #19869) and filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (`session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`, seat post #6017). Devs do not open issues. ⛔ Filed bare: routing and grading belong to triage. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What the declaration says, two ways

Read by this seat at source on `origin/main` `b940f32a56`:

| face | text |
|:--|:--|
| the regex, `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` | `/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/`: EVERY dot-separated segment must open with a lowercase letter |
| the refusal, `manifestIdRefusal(key, input)` | 「Invalid package id '…' on `key`. Expected reverse-domain notation (examples) — lowercase dot-separated segments; hyphens allowed inside a segment, underscores are not.」 |

⇒ `com.example.2app` and `com.2example.app` satisfy every clause the sentence states, and the regex refuses both. The implementing round measured them from source on `0e90a8d1c5`: both are refused with exactly that sentence and no repair suggestion, and `com.example.-app` is refused the same way. That half is the round's reading; this seat re-read the pattern and the sentence, and ⛔ did not re-run the probe.

## Who reads the sentence

It is runtime text shipped to authors, surfaced at every door that validates a package id:
- `ManifestSchema.id` (`manifest.id`);
- `PackageSchema.manifestId` (the publish payload), in `marketplace/package.zod.ts`;
- `metadata-protocol`'s install and duplicate doors (`targetPackageId`) and `runtime`'s install domain, which hand it back verbatim.

Tests in `metadata-protocol` and `runtime` compare against `manifestIdRefusal(...)` itself, ⛔ not a literal, so a reworded sentence flows through them.

NORTH-STAR rule 4: 「错的必须被响亮拒绝并给处方」. The refusal is loud, but its prescription is incomplete.

## Suggested shape (⛔ not a ruling)

Make the sentence state the rule the regex enforces, e.g. 「… lowercase dot-separated segments, each starting with a letter; hyphens allowed inside a segment, underscores are not.」 Keep the regex unchanged; this is text only.

## Filing-gate answers

- **Class**: ① (defect, named landing site); finding class (c).
- **Producer**: authors writing `manifest.id` (`defineStack`, `os build`), and the publish payload's `manifestId`.
- **Dedupe**, MCP issue search in this repo, closed included, at 2026-09-23T14:05Z:
  - `manifest.id refusal segment must start with a letter leading digit`: 1 hit, #19831 (the namespace sibling, a different key).
  - `manifestIdRefusal MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN reverse-domain package id`: 4 hits (#19417, #19576, #17534, #16520). All are about which doors enforce the pattern, and none is about the sentence omitting the leading-letter rule.

Dedupe words: `manifestIdRefusal segment must start with a letter` · `manifest.id refusal leading digit segment` · `reverse-domain refusal omits leading-letter rule`
